title: Microsoft Purview: auto-labeling ceiling for SharePoint and OneDrive rises to 500,000 files a day (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: Hold: the briefing promises that existing policies receive the higher ceiling without administrator action, although the sources do not state the arrival behaviour. It also says auto-labeling applies document markings, which Microsoft explicitly says these policies do not apply. The roadmap details, licensing, commands and documented throughput limits otherwise check out.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the increase's arrival behaviour or whether it requires administrator action, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: auto-labeling scale increase administrator 500,000. Read both roadmap records, Learn's apply-sensitivity-label-automatically page and relevant search excerpts; none states how the increase activates or whether administrator action is needed.

claims.claim: Auto-labeling policies run continuously until deleted.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling policies run continuously until they're deleted.

claims.claim: New and modified files are included under the current policy settings.
claims.quote: For example, new and modified files will be included with the current policy settings.

claims.claim: For tenants with policies already turned on, the ceiling rises without changing a policy.
claims.quote: Searched: auto-labeling scale increase administrator 500,000; Purview auto-labeling 500,000 throughput ceiling setting administrator action default price meter. Read the roadmap and Learn auto-labeling guidance; neither states that existing policies receive the increase without administrator action.
claims.fix: Replace the opening sentence of Why it matters with: 'For tenants with auto-labeling policies already turned on, the higher ceiling could allow more files to be labelled each day; Microsoft has not stated whether the increase requires administrator action.' This also removes the conflict with defaultState unknown and the following paragraph.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the increase helps protect existing content sooner and prepare data for Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: With sensitivity labels and protection settings applied to more files sooner, organizations can better prepare their data estate for Microsoft 365 Copilot with greater confidence.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Auto-labeling can apply a label's encryption to SharePoint and OneDrive files.
claims.quote: When the auto-labeling policy includes locations for SharePoint or OneDrive, the label must be configured for the Assign permissions now setting, and User access to content expires must be set to Never.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Service-side auto-labeling applies a label's markings to SharePoint and OneDrive documents.
claims.quote: If the labels you select are configured to use visual markings (headers, footers, watermarks), these markings aren't applied to documents when you use auto-labeling.
claims.fix: Replace the first Data exposure sentence with: 'Policies that are on can label more files a day, and where a label applies encryption, its protection can reach more content sooner.' In the impact rationale, remove 'or markings'. Learn explicitly excludes document visual markings: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/apply-sensitivity-label-automatically.

claims.claim: When a label encrypts a file, the Rights Management issuer and owner is the account that last modified it.
claims.quote: When the label applies encryption, the Rights Management issuer and Rights Management owner is the account that last modified the file.

claims.claim: Users do not participate in service-side labeling, so an enforcing policy does not wait for their review.
claims.quote: Because the user doesn't interact with the labeling process, auto-labeling policies don't support recommended labeling

claims.claim: Auto-labeling policies do not support recommended labeling.
claims.quote: auto-labeling policies don't support recommended labeling

claims.claim: Microsoft advises simulation and refinement before turning on a policy.
claims.quote: Review the results, and if necessary, refine your policy. ... Rerun simulation mode and wait for it to complete again.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The labeling progress information updates every 48 hours.
claims.quote: This progress information updates every 48 hours, so you can expect to see the most current data about every other day.

claims.claim: Auto-labeling does not change existing modified, modified by or date values on a file.
claims.quote: Existing values for modified, modified by, and the date aren't changed as a result of auto-labeling policies—for both simulation mode and when labels are applied.
